#   BEEGFS_MOUNT         overrides --mount-point default (/mnt/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT     host dir for container-side target storage (/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG     image tag for ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-* (7.4.6)
#   BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT  seconds to wait for mgmtd to become reachable (60)
#
# Exit code == command's exit code. Teardown runs on any exit.

set -eu

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"

MNT="${BEEGFS_MOUNT:-/mnt/beegfs}"
DATA_ROOT="${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}"
COMPOSE="$repo_root/beegfs/docker-compose.yml"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$repo_root/beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template"
CONF_ACTIVE="/etc/beegfs/beegfs-client-test.conf"
STARTUP_WAIT="${BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT:-60}"
KEEP=0
SET_HOME=0

usage() {
  sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit "${1:-2}"
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    --mount-point) MNT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --set-home) SET_HOME=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage 0 ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; usage 2 ;;
  esac
done

[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "no command given" >&2; usage 2; }

SUDO=""
if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
  command -v sudo >/dev/null || {
    echo "must run as root (or have sudo available)" >&2; exit 2; }
  SUDO="sudo"
fi

log() { printf '\nI: %s\n' "$*"; }

ensure_client_installed() {
  if modinfo beegfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  echo "ERROR: beegfs kernel module not available." >&2
  echo "  Install with: apt install beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils" >&2
  exit 3
}

start_cluster() {
  log "creating data dirs under $DATA_ROOT"
  $SUDO mkdir -p \
    "$DATA_ROOT/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/meta_01_tgt_0101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_102"

  log "docker compose up (BeeGFS ${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6})"
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
  BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG="${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}" \
    $SUDO -E docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" up -d

  log "waiting up to ${STARTUP_WAIT}s for mgmtd on tcp/8008"
  local waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -lt "$STARTUP_WAIT" ]; do
    # mgmtd listens on 8008/tcp once initialised. `ss` is in iproute2.
    if $SUDO ss -ltn "sport = :8008" 2>/dev/null | grep -q :8008; then
      log "mgmtd is up (after ${waited}s)"
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
  done
  echo "ERROR: mgmtd did not come up within ${STARTUP_WAIT}s" >&2
  $SUDO docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" logs --tail=200 >&2 || true
  exit 4
}

write_client_conf() {
  log "writing $CONF_ACTIVE"
  $SUDO install -d /etc/beegfs
  $SUDO install -m 0644 "$CONF_TEMPLATE" "$CONF_ACTIVE"
}

mount_beegfs() {
  log "starting beegfs-helperd"
  # helperd reads the same conf; point it at ours.
  $SUDO systemctl start beegfs-helperd || {
    # No systemd (e.g. inside `act` container): fall back to direct launch.
    $SUDO beegfs-helperd cfgFile="$CONF_ACTIVE" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    sleep 1
  }

  log "mounting BeeGFS at $MNT"
  $SUDO mkdir -p "$MNT"
  $SUDO mount -t beegfs beegfs_nodev "$MNT" -o "cfgFile=$CONF_ACTIVE"
  $SUDO chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$MNT"
  $SUDO mount | grep -F "$MNT" | sed 's/^/I: /'
}

teardown() {
  local rc=$?
  set +e
  if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ]; then
    echo "I: --keep set; leaving cluster + mount up (exit=$rc)"
    return "$rc"
  fi
  log "teardown"
  $SUDO umount "$MNT" 2>/dev/null || true
  $SUDO systemctl stop beegfs-helperd 2>/dev/null || $SUDO pkill -f beegfs-helperd || true
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
    $SUDO -E docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" down -v 2>/dev/null || true
  $SUDO rm -rf "$DATA_ROOT" "$CONF_ACTIVE"
  return "$rc"
}
trap teardown EXIT

ensure_client_installed
start_cluster
write_client_conf
mount_beegfs

RUN_HOME="$HOME"
if [ "$SET_HOME" = 1 ]; then
  RUN_HOME="$MNT/home"
  mkdir -p "$RUN_HOME"
fi

log "running: $*"
HOME="$RUN_HOME" TMPDIR="$MNT" DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR="$MNT" "$@"

name: BeeGFS harness smoke test

# Proves eval_under_beegfs works end-to-end on a real ubuntu-24.04 GH runner.
# Not a git-annex regression test -- that lives in the drafts/ workflow which
# is meant to be merged into datalad/git-annex.

    paths:
      - "tools/**"
      - "beegfs/**"
      - "provision/**"
      - ".github/workflows/smoke.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 5 * * 1"  # weekly Mon 05:17 UTC -- catches upstream image drift

jobs:

      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        beegfs-version: ["7.4.6"]

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install BeeGFS client (DKMS) + utils
        env:
          BEEGFS_VERSION: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo_ver="${BEEGFS_VERSION%.*}"
          codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
          list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/dists/beegfs-${codename}.list"
          curl -fsI "$list_url" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/dists/beegfs-jammy.list"
          sudo curl -fsSL "$list_url" -o /etc/apt/sources.list.d/beegfs.list
          sudo curl -fsSL "https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/gpg/GPG-KEY-beegfs" \
            -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/beegfs.asc
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            dkms "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" \
            beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils
          modinfo beegfs

      - name: Install git-annex
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git-annex
          git-annex version | head -3

      - name: Smoke-test eval_under_beegfs
        env:
          BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo -E ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- bash -eu -c '
            echo "HOME=$HOME  TMPDIR=$TMPDIR"
            mount | grep -F "$TMPDIR"
            cd "$HOME"
            git config --global user.email test@example.com
            git config --global user.name  test
            git init t
            cd t
            git annex init smoke
            dd if=/dev/urandom of=big bs=1M count=10 status=none
            git annex add big
            git commit -m "add big"
            git annex fsck
            echo OK
          '

      - name: Container logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: sudo docker compose -f beegfs/docker-compose.yml logs --tail=500 || true

input.content:
# beegfs-test

Development harness for testing git-annex (and, later, DataLad) under
[BeeGFS](https://www.beegfs.io/), driven from GitHub Actions. Scratch repo
for iteration; the parts destined for upstream get PR'd to their real
homes (see below).

**Why**. A 2024 report of [35+ git-annex test failures on
BeeGFS 7.4.6](https://git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/)
tracked back to file-descriptor leakage across `rename()` — a class of bug
that BeeGFS's rename semantics expose but ext4/tmpfs/NFS usually mask. We
want ongoing CI coverage on BeeGFS so the next regression of this class
gets caught. Related upstream ask:
[ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers#21](https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers/issues/21).

## Layout

| Path                                    | Purpose                                                                |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Vagrantfile` + `provision/`            | Ubuntu 24.04 libvirt VM with docker + BeeGFS client + git-annex        |
| `beegfs/docker-compose.yml`             | BeeGFS v7 test cluster (mgmtd + meta + storage), `network_mode: host`  |
| `beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template`    | Minimal client conf pointing at localhost, no auth                     |
| `tools/eval_under_beegfs`               | Wrapper: bring up cluster, mount, run cmd with `TMPDIR` on BeeGFS      |
| `.github/workflows/smoke.yaml`          | End-to-end sanity of the harness on a real GH runner                   |
| `drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml`     | Copy-target workflow for `datalad/git-annex`                           |

## Local iteration (VM)

The dev container this repo is usually edited in lacks `CAP_SYS_MODULE`, so
the BeeGFS client kmod cannot be loaded there. Use the Vagrant VM:

```bash
vagrant up                              # first time: ~10 min
vagrant ssh
cd /vagrant

# Smoke:
sudo ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- bash -c '
  cd "$HOME"
  git init t && cd t
  git annex init && echo hi > f && git annex add f && git annex fsck
'

# Full run (may find real bugs -- that IS the point):
sudo ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- timeout 3600 bash -c 'cd "$HOME" && git annex test'
```

Optional: install `act` in the VM to replay the GitHub workflow locally.

```bash
VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT=1 vagrant provision
vagrant ssh -c 'cd /vagrant && act -j smoke'
```

`act` runs the workflow in a container, so it can validate the YAML flow
but cannot exercise the BeeGFS kernel module — it's useful for shaking out
workflow bugs, not for actual filesystem testing.

## `eval_under_beegfs` in one paragraph

Mirrors the shape of [`datalad/datalad
tools/eval_under_nfs`](https://github.com/datalad/datalad/blob/maint/tools/eval_under_nfs):
takes a command, wraps setup + teardown around it, and runs the command
with `TMPDIR`, `DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR` (and optionally `HOME`) pointing
at the BeeGFS mount. Exit code passes through. Teardown runs from a
`trap` on any exit. Use `--keep` to inspect state after a failure.

## Upstream targets

- `tools/eval_under_beegfs` + `beegfs/*` + a copy of
  `drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml` → PR to
  [datalad/git-annex](https://github.com/datalad/git-annex) once validated,
  either as a new workflow or as a matrix flavor of
  `test-annex` in `build-ubuntu.yaml`.
- Optionally, a slimmed-down smoke workflow → PR to
  [ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers](https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers)
  addressing their [issue #21](https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers/issues/21).

## Requirements (host, for Vagrant)

- libvirt + `vagrant-libvirt` plugin (Debian/Ubuntu:
  `apt install vagrant libvirt-daemon-system` then
  `vagrant plugin install vagrant-libvirt`)
- ~30 GB free disk, ~6 GB free RAM for the VM

## References

- Bug that motivated this: <https://git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/>
- BeeGFS containerisation guidance: <https://doc.beegfs.io/latest/advanced_topics/containers.html>

# beegfs-test

Development harness for testing git-annex (and, later, DataLad) under
[BeeGFS](https://www.beegfs.io/), driven from GitHub Actions. Scratch repo
for iteration; the parts destined for upstream get PR'd to their real
homes (see below).

**Why**. A 2024 report of [35+ git-annex test failures on
BeeGFS 7.4.6](https://git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/)
tracked back to file-descriptor leakage across `rename()` — a class of bug
that BeeGFS's rename semantics expose but ext4/tmpfs/NFS usually mask. We
want ongoing CI coverage on BeeGFS so the next regression of this class
gets caught. Related upstream ask:
[ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers#21](https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers/issues/21).

## Layout

| Path                                    | Purpose                                                                |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Vagrantfile` + `provision/`            | Ubuntu 24.04 libvirt VM with docker + BeeGFS client + git-annex        |
| `beegfs/docker-compose.yml`             | BeeGFS v7 test cluster (mgmtd + meta + storage), `network_mode: host`  |
| `beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template`    | Minimal client conf pointing at localhost, no auth                     |
| `tools/eval_under_beegfs`               | Wrapper: bring up cluster, mount, run cmd with `TMPDIR` on BeeGFS      |
| `.github/workflows/smoke.yaml`          | End-to-end sanity of the harness on a real GH runner                   |
| `drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml`     | Copy-target workflow for `datalad/git-annex`                           |

## Local iteration (VM)

The dev container this repo is usually edited in lacks `CAP_SYS_MODULE`, so
the BeeGFS client kmod cannot be loaded there. Use the Vagrant VM:

```bash
vagrant up                              # first time: ~10 min
vagrant ssh
cd /vagrant

# Smoke:
sudo ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- bash -c '
  cd "$HOME"
  git init t && cd t
  git annex init && echo hi > f && git annex add f && git annex fsck
'

# Full run (may find real bugs -- that IS the point):
sudo ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- timeout 3600 bash -c 'cd "$HOME" && git annex test'
```

Optional: install `act` in the VM to replay the GitHub workflow locally.

```bash
VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT=1 vagrant provision
vagrant ssh -c 'cd /vagrant && act -j smoke'
```

`act` runs the workflow in a container, so it can validate the YAML flow
but cannot exercise the BeeGFS kernel module — it's useful for shaking out
workflow bugs, not for actual filesystem testing.

## `eval_under_beegfs` in one paragraph

Mirrors the shape of [`datalad/datalad
tools/eval_under_nfs`](https://github.com/datalad/datalad/blob/maint/tools/eval_under_nfs):
takes a command, wraps setup + teardown around it, and runs the command
with `TMPDIR`, `DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR` (and optionally `HOME`) pointing
at the BeeGFS mount. Exit code passes through. Teardown runs from a
`trap` on any exit. Use `--keep` to inspect state after a failure.

## Upstream targets

- `tools/eval_under_beegfs` + `beegfs/*` + a copy of
  `drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml` → PR to
  [datalad/git-annex](https://github.com/datalad/git-annex) once validated,
  either as a new workflow or as a matrix flavor of
  `test-annex` in `build-ubuntu.yaml`.
- Optionally, a slimmed-down smoke workflow → PR to
  [ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers](https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers)
  addressing their [issue #21](https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers/issues/21).

## Requirements (host, for Vagrant)

- libvirt + `vagrant-libvirt` plugin (Debian/Ubuntu:
  `apt install vagrant libvirt-daemon-system` then
  `vagrant plugin install vagrant-libvirt`)
- ~30 GB free disk, ~6 GB free RAM for the VM

## References

- Bug that motivated this: <https://git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/>

- BeeGFS CSI driver e2e workflow (client install patterns):
  <https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-csi-driver/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-test-publish.yaml>

# -*- mode: ruby -*-
# vi: set ft=ruby :
#
# Vagrantfile for developing/testing the beegfs-test harness locally.
#
# Provides an Ubuntu 24.04 VM with Docker + BeeGFS client kernel module +
# git-annex, so a dev container without CAP_SYS_MODULE can iterate on the
# eval_under_beegfs wrapper and GH workflows.
#
# Default provider: libvirt (KVM/QEMU). Falls back gracefully if unset.
#
# Env vars:
#   VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT=1   also install nektos/act for local workflow replays
#   BEEGFS_VERSION=7.4.6    BeeGFS APT repo version to use (default 7.4.6)

Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
  config.vm.box = "generic/ubuntu2404"
  config.vm.hostname = "beegfs-test"

  # Sync the repo into the guest. rsync is more portable than 9p/virtiofs
  # and avoids permission surprises when root inside the VM touches files.
  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/vagrant", type: "rsync",
    rsync__exclude: [".git/", ".datalad/", ".vagrant/"]

  config.vm.provider :libvirt do |lv|
    lv.cpus = 4
    lv.memory = 6144
    lv.machine_virtual_size = 30
    lv.cpu_mode = "host-passthrough"
    lv.nested = true
  end

  config.vm.provider :virtualbox do |vb|
    vb.cpus = 4
    vb.memory = 6144
  end

  beegfs_version = ENV.fetch("BEEGFS_VERSION", "7.4.6")

  config.vm.provision "setup", type: "shell",
    path: "provision/setup.sh",
    env: { "BEEGFS_VERSION" => beegfs_version },
    privileged: true

  if ENV["VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT"] == "1"
    config.vm.provision "act", type: "shell",
      path: "provision/install-act.sh",
      privileged: true
  end
end

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Yaroslav Halchenko <yaroslav.o.halchenko@dartmouth.edu>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Generated with Claude Code 2.1.63 / Claude Opus 4.7
#
# Provision an Ubuntu 24.04 VM to develop/test the beegfs-test harness:
#   - Docker CE + compose plugin
#   - BeeGFS client kernel module (DKMS) + helperd + utils
#   - git-annex + git (Ubuntu apt versions, enough to smoke-test the wrapper)
#
# Idempotent: safe to re-run via `vagrant provision`.

set -euo pipefail

BEEGFS_VERSION="${BEEGFS_VERSION:-7.4.6}"
# Major.minor is what the beegfs APT repo layout uses (e.g. "7.4").
BEEGFS_REPO_VER="${BEEGFS_VERSION%.*}"

log() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$*"; }

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

log "Base packages"
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release \
  build-essential dkms "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" \
  git git-annex jq

log "Docker CE + compose plugin"
if ! command -v docker >/dev/null; then
  install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
  curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg \
    -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
  echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $codename stable" \
    > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
fi
usermod -aG docker vagrant || true
systemctl enable --now docker

log "BeeGFS APT repo (v${BEEGFS_REPO_VER})"
# Prefer a list file for the current Ubuntu codename; fall back to jammy
# if the newer codename isn't yet published (BeeGFS DKMS still builds).
codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_REPO_VER}/dists/beegfs-${codename}.list"
if ! curl -fsI "$list_url" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "beegfs-${codename}.list not published upstream; falling back to jammy" >&2
  list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_REPO_VER}/dists/beegfs-jammy.list"
fi
curl -fsSL "$list_url" -o /etc/apt/sources.list.d/beegfs.list
curl -fsSL "https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_REPO_VER}/gpg/GPG-KEY-beegfs" \
  -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/beegfs.asc
apt-get update -qq

log "BeeGFS client (DKMS) + helperd + utils"
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils

# Verify the DKMS module built and is loadable. modprobe --dry-run avoids
# actually loading (that happens at mount time), so it's safe to fail-fast
# here if the module wasn't produced.
if ! modinfo beegfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: beegfs kernel module was not built by DKMS." >&2
  dkms status || true
  exit 1
fi

# helperd disabled by default — eval_under_beegfs starts it on demand.
systemctl disable --now beegfs-helperd || true

log "Provisioning complete"
echo "  git-annex : $(git-annex version | head -1)"

echo "  beegfs mod: $(modinfo -F version beegfs 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"

name: BeeGFS harness smoke test

# Proves eval_under_beegfs works end-to-end on a real ubuntu-24.04 GH runner.
# Not a git-annex regression test -- that lives in the drafts/ workflow which
# is meant to be merged into datalad/git-annex.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
    paths:
      - "tools/**"
      - "beegfs/**"
      - "provision/**"
      - ".github/workflows/smoke.yaml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "tools/**"
      - "beegfs/**"
      - "provision/**"
      - ".github/workflows/smoke.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 5 * * 1"  # weekly Mon 05:17 UTC -- catches upstream image drift

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        beegfs-version: ["7.4.6"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install BeeGFS client (DKMS) + utils
        env:
          BEEGFS_VERSION: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo_ver="${BEEGFS_VERSION%.*}"
          codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
          list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/dists/beegfs-${codename}.list"
          curl -fsI "$list_url" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/dists/beegfs-jammy.list"
          sudo curl -fsSL "$list_url" -o /etc/apt/sources.list.d/beegfs.list
          sudo curl -fsSL "https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/gpg/GPG-KEY-beegfs" \
            -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/beegfs.asc
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            dkms "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" \
            beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils
          modinfo beegfs

      - name: Install git-annex
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git-annex
          git-annex version | head -3

      - name: Smoke-test eval_under_beegfs
        env:
          BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo -E ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- bash -eu -c '
            echo "HOME=$HOME  TMPDIR=$TMPDIR"
            mount | grep -F "$TMPDIR"
            cd "$HOME"
            git config --global user.email test@example.com
            git config --global user.name  test
            git init t
            cd t
            git annex init smoke
            dd if=/dev/urandom of=big bs=1M count=10 status=none
            git annex add big
            git commit -m "add big"
            git annex fsck
            echo OK
          '

      - name: Container logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: sudo docker compose -f beegfs/docker-compose.yml logs --tail=500 || true

# DRAFT: standalone job to drop into datalad/git-annex/.github/workflows/
# as either a new file (test-beegfs.yaml) or a new job appended to
# build-ubuntu.yaml alongside test-annex / test-annex-more.
#
# Design decision (see plan): kept as a separate job (not a matrix flavor)
# because BeeGFS setup adds ~3-5 min of prep unrelated to the other flavors
# and an independent failure signal is easier to triage.
#
# Depends on the same build-package job that test-annex uses -- reuses the
# built .deb via download-artifact.
#
# When merging upstream:
#   1. Copy this file to datalad/git-annex/.github/workflows/test-beegfs.yaml
#      (or splice the `test-annex-beegfs:` job into build-ubuntu.yaml).
#   2. Add eval_under_beegfs + beegfs/ dir to datalad/git-annex under
#      .github/workflows/tools/  (mirroring the setup_crippledfs layout).
#   3. Adjust the tools/ path in the `Run tests` step accordingly.

name: Test git-annex on BeeGFS

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  # In-repo, this is usually chained after build-package via `needs:`.
  # Left as workflow_dispatch here so the draft is standalone-runnable
  # for validation via actionlint / act.

jobs:
  test-annex-beegfs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 90
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        beegfs-version: ["7.4.6"]
        # When splicing into build-ubuntu.yaml, add `needs: build-package`
        # and download the freshly-built .deb instead of installing from apt.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install BeeGFS client (DKMS) + utils
        env:
          BEEGFS_VERSION: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo_ver="${BEEGFS_VERSION%.*}"
          codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
          list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/dists/beegfs-${codename}.list"
          curl -fsI "$list_url" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/dists/beegfs-jammy.list"
          sudo curl -fsSL "$list_url" -o /etc/apt/sources.list.d/beegfs.list
          sudo curl -fsSL "https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${repo_ver}/gpg/GPG-KEY-beegfs" \
            -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/beegfs.asc
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            dkms "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" \
            beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils
          modinfo beegfs

      # UPSTREAM CHANGE: replace this step with the existing pattern from
      # build-ubuntu.yaml (download-artifact + dpkg -i git-annex*.deb).
      - name: Install git-annex (apt; draft only)
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git-annex
          git annex version | head -5

      - name: Configure git identity
        run: |
          git config --global user.email test@github.land
          git config --global user.name  "GitHub Almighty"

      - name: Run git annex test under BeeGFS
        env:
          BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        # --set-home mirrors the *-home flavors in build-ubuntu.yaml
        # (HOME on the tested FS; catches the class of bugs seen in
        # git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/).
        run: |
          sudo -E ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- \
            timeout 3600 bash -c 'cd "$HOME" && git annex test'

      - name: Container logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: sudo docker compose -f beegfs/docker-compose.yml logs --tail=500 || true

"""Complete a Keycloak device-flow login in a headless browser.

Usage: kc_playwright_login.py <verification_uri> <user_code> <username> <password>
"""
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, TimeoutError as PWTimeout


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 5:
        print("usage: kc_playwright_login.py <uri> <code> <user> <pass>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    uri, code, username, password = sys.argv[1:]
    shots = Path("/tmp/kc_shots")
    shots.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    with sync_playwright() as p:
        b = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        ctx = b.new_context(ignore_https_errors=True, viewport={"width": 1200, "height": 900})
        page = ctx.new_page()

        print(f"[1/4] GET {uri}")
        page.goto(uri, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
        page.screenshot(path=str(shots / "1-device-form.png"))

        # Device-code entry
        page.fill("#device_user_code", code)
        page.screenshot(path=str(shots / "2-code-filled.png"))
        print(f"[2/4] submit user_code={code}")
        page.click("#kc-login")

        # Login form
        page.wait_for_selector("#username", timeout=15000)
        page.fill("#username", username)
        page.fill("#password", password)
        page.screenshot(path=str(shots / "3-login-filled.png"))
        print(f"[3/4] submit login user={username}")
        page.click("#kc-login")

        # Consent / device confirm — button varies by theme; try common ones.
        # Newer Keycloak: "Grant Access" / "Deny Access". We want to accept.
        try:
            page.wait_for_selector(
                "input[name=accept], button[name=accept], #kc-login, [value=Yes], text=/Grant|Yes|Accept|Continue/i",
                timeout=10000,
            )
        except PWTimeout:
            pass
        page.screenshot(path=str(shots / "4-consent.png"))

        for sel in (
            "input[name=accept]",
            "button[name=accept]",
            "input[value=Yes]",
            "button:has-text('Grant Access')",
            "button:has-text('Accept')",
            "button:has-text('Yes')",
            "#kc-login",  # some themes just show a login-styled confirm
        ):
            try:
                el = page.locator(sel).first
                if el.count() and el.is_visible():
                    print(f"[4/4] click consent via {sel!r}")
                    el.click()
                    break
            except Exception:
                pass

        # give the redirect / success page a moment
        time.sleep(2)
        page.screenshot(path=str(shots / "5-final.png"))
        print(f"[done] final title={page.title()!r}, url={page.url}")
        b.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# -*- mode: ruby -*-
# vi: set ft=ruby :
#
# Vagrantfile for developing/testing the beegfs-test harness locally.
#
# Provides an Ubuntu 24.04 VM with Docker + BeeGFS client kernel module +
# git-annex, so a dev container without CAP_SYS_MODULE can iterate on the
# eval_under_beegfs wrapper and GH workflows.
#
# Default provider: libvirt (KVM/QEMU). Falls back gracefully if unset.
#
# Env vars:
#   VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT=1   also install nektos/act for local workflow replays
#   BEEGFS_VERSION=7.4.6    BeeGFS APT repo version to use (default 7.4.6)

Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
  # Box choice depends on provider:
  #   libvirt      -> cloud-image/ubuntu-24.04  (Canonical official; also has qemu)
  #   virtualbox   -> bento/ubuntu-24.04        (no libvirt provider available)
  # generic/* boxes were retired from Vagrant Cloud in 2024.
  provider = ENV["VAGRANT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER"] || "libvirt"
  config.vm.box = case provider
                  when "virtualbox" then "bento/ubuntu-24.04"
                  else "cloud-image/ubuntu-24.04"
                  end
  config.vm.hostname = "beegfs-test"

  # Sync the repo into the guest. rsync is more portable than 9p/virtiofs
  # and avoids permission surprises when root inside the VM touches files.
  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/vagrant", type: "rsync",
    rsync__exclude: [".git/", ".datalad/", ".vagrant/"]

  config.vm.provider :libvirt do |lv|
    lv.cpus = 4
    lv.memory = 6144
    lv.machine_virtual_size = 30
    lv.cpu_mode = "host-passthrough"
    lv.nested = true
  end

  config.vm.provider :virtualbox do |vb|
    vb.cpus = 4
    vb.memory = 6144
  end

  beegfs_version = ENV.fetch("BEEGFS_VERSION", "7.4.6")

  config.vm.provision "setup", type: "shell",
    path: "provision/setup.sh",
    env: { "BEEGFS_VERSION" => beegfs_version },
    privileged: true

  if ENV["VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT"] == "1"
    config.vm.provision "act", type: "shell",
      path: "provision/install-act.sh",
      privileged: true
  end
end

---
name: SSH into a Vagrant/libvirt VM from Claude's dev container
description: How to reach yoh's Vagrant-libvirt VMs directly from inside the container Claude runs in (bilena workstation)
type: reference
---

Claude's dev container on yoh's `bilena` workstation has only a `tun0` VPN
interface (10.229.128.x/32) with a `default dev tun0` route. Everything
routes through the VPN. The libvirt-default NAT range (192.168.121.0/24)
is NOT carried by the VPN in practice — SSH to it times out.

**The 172.28.128.0/24 subnet IS routed by the VPN back to the host's
libvirt bridge.** This was originally set up for the `datalad_in_a_box`
project (Vagrantfile added `private_network ip: "172.28.128.42"`, and
the network is/was named `diab-priv`). Any Vagrant VM given a static IP
on that subnet becomes directly SSH-able from Claude's container.

## Pattern

In the Vagrantfile:

```ruby
vm_ip = ENV.fetch("<PROJECT>_VM_IP", "172.28.128.<N>")   # pick N != 42
config.vm.network "private_network", ip: vm_ip
```

Then from the container:

```bash
ssh -i <PROJECT>/.vagrant/machines/default/libvirt/private_key \
    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
    -o UserKnownHostsFile=/tmp/<PROJECT>-known_hosts \
    -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
    vagrant@172.28.128.<N> 'CMD'
```

Applying `private_network` to an already-running VM requires
`vagrant reload` (or `vagrant halt && vagrant up`).

## Gotchas learned

- `generic/ubuntu2404` was retired from Vagrant Cloud in 2024. For
  libvirt use `cloud-image/ubuntu-24.04` (Canonical official).
  `bento/ubuntu-24.04` has no libvirt provider — VirtualBox only.
- vagrant-libvirt matches `private_network` by SUBNET, not by name. If
  another project's network already covers 172.28.128.0/24 (like
  diab-priv), your VM silently attaches to it — usually fine, but the
  domain XML records that other network's name, so if it's inactive at
  boot, libvirt refuses to start your VM. To force a dedicated bridge:
  `libvirt__network_name: "<project>-priv"` — but a dedicated bridge
  is not routed by the VPN, defeating the purpose. Reuse the shared
  subnet unless you have a reason not to.
- Pick an unused last octet. `.42` is diab's; `.50` and up are safe.

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Yaroslav Halchenko <yaroslav.o.halchenko@dartmouth.edu>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Generated with Claude Code 2.1.63 / Claude Opus 4.7
#
# Evaluate a command with TMPDIR / DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR (and optionally
# HOME) pointing at a BeeGFS mount, backed by a containerised BeeGFS cluster
# (mgmtd + meta + storage) brought up via docker compose.
#
# Modelled on datalad/datalad tools/eval_under_nfs -- same wrapper shape so
# CI usage matches: `eval_under_beegfs -- timeout 3600 git annex test`.
#
# Usage:
#   eval_under_beegfs [--keep] [--mount-point PATH] [--set-home] -- CMD [ARGS...]
#
#   --keep         skip teardown (leave containers + mount alive for debugging)
#   --mount-point  where to mount BeeGFS on host (default /mnt/beegfs)
#   --set-home     also set HOME=<mount-point>/home (mimics the git-annex
#                  build-ubuntu.yaml `*-home` flavors)
#
# Env vars:
#   BEEGFS_MOUNT         overrides --mount-point default (/mnt/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT     host dir for container-side target storage (/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG     image tag for ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-* (7.4.6)
#   BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT  seconds to wait for mgmtd to become reachable (60)
#
# Exit code == command's exit code. Teardown runs on any exit.

set -eu

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"

MNT="${BEEGFS_MOUNT:-/mnt/beegfs}"
DATA_ROOT="${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}"
COMPOSE="$repo_root/beegfs/docker-compose.yml"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$repo_root/beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template"
CONF_ACTIVE="/etc/beegfs/beegfs-client-test.conf"
STARTUP_WAIT="${BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT:-60}"
KEEP=0
SET_HOME=0

usage() {
  sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit "${1:-2}"
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    --mount-point) MNT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --set-home) SET_HOME=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage 0 ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; usage 2 ;;
  esac
done

[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "no command given" >&2; usage 2; }

SUDO=""
if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
  command -v sudo >/dev/null || {
    echo "must run as root (or have sudo available)" >&2; exit 2; }
  SUDO="sudo"
fi

log() { printf '\nI: %s\n' "$*"; }

ensure_client_installed() {
  if modinfo beegfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  echo "ERROR: beegfs kernel module not available." >&2
  echo "  Install with: apt install beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils" >&2
  exit 3
}

start_cluster() {
  log "creating data dirs under $DATA_ROOT"
  $SUDO mkdir -p \
    "$DATA_ROOT/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/meta_01_tgt_0101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_102"

  log "docker compose up (BeeGFS ${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6})"
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
  BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG="${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}" \
    $SUDO -E docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" up -d

  log "waiting up to ${STARTUP_WAIT}s for mgmtd on tcp/8008"
  local waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -lt "$STARTUP_WAIT" ]; do
    # mgmtd listens on 8008/tcp once initialised. `ss` is in iproute2.
    if $SUDO ss -ltn "sport = :8008" 2>/dev/null | grep -q :8008; then
      log "mgmtd is up (after ${waited}s)"
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
  done
  echo "ERROR: mgmtd did not come up within ${STARTUP_WAIT}s" >&2
  $SUDO docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" logs --tail=200 >&2 || true
  exit 4
}

write_client_conf() {
  log "writing $CONF_ACTIVE"
  $SUDO install -d /etc/beegfs
  $SUDO install -m 0644 "$CONF_TEMPLATE" "$CONF_ACTIVE"
}

mount_beegfs() {
  log "starting beegfs-helperd"
  # helperd reads the same conf; point it at ours.
  $SUDO systemctl start beegfs-helperd || {
    # No systemd (e.g. inside `act` container): fall back to direct launch.
    $SUDO beegfs-helperd cfgFile="$CONF_ACTIVE" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    sleep 1
  }

  log "mounting BeeGFS at $MNT"
  $SUDO mkdir -p "$MNT"
  $SUDO mount -t beegfs beegfs_nodev "$MNT" -o "cfgFile=$CONF_ACTIVE"
  $SUDO chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$MNT"
  $SUDO mount | grep -F "$MNT" | sed 's/^/I: /'
}

teardown() {
  local rc=$?
  set +e
  if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ]; then
    echo "I: --keep set; leaving cluster + mount up (exit=$rc)"
    return "$rc"
  fi
  log "teardown"
  $SUDO umount "$MNT" 2>/dev/null || true
  $SUDO systemctl stop beegfs-helperd 2>/dev/null || $SUDO pkill -f beegfs-helperd || true
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
    $SUDO -E docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" down -v 2>/dev/null || true
  $SUDO rm -rf "$DATA_ROOT" "$CONF_ACTIVE"
  return "$rc"
}
trap teardown EXIT

ensure_client_installed
start_cluster
write_client_conf
mount_beegfs

RUN_HOME="$HOME"
if [ "$SET_HOME" = 1 ]; then
  RUN_HOME="$MNT/home"
  mkdir -p "$RUN_HOME"
fi

log "running: $*"
HOME="$RUN_HOME" TMPDIR="$MNT" DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR="$MNT" "$@"

# BeeGFS v7 test cluster for eval_under_beegfs.
#
# Derived from ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers examples/docker-compose-v7.yml,
# modified for host-mode networking so the beegfs kernel client on the host
# can reach mgmtd/meta/storage on localhost. See:
#   https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers/issues/21
#   https://doc.beegfs.io/latest/advanced_topics/containers.html
#
# BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT (default /beegfs) chooses where target dirs live on host.
# BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG pins the ghcr.io/thinkparq/* image tag. Override for a
# specific point release; default follows the v7 line.

services:
  beegfs-management:
    image: ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-mgmtd:${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}
    container_name: beegfs-mgmtd
    privileged: true
    network_mode: host
    command: >-
      storeMgmtdDirectory=/mnt/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01
      storeAllowFirstRunInit=false
      connMgmtdPortTCP=8008
      connMgmtdPortUDP=8008
    environment:
      - beegfs_setup_1=beegfs-setup-mgmtd -p /mnt/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01 -C -S mgmt_tgt_mgmt01
    volumes:
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01:/mnt/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01

  beegfs-meta:
    image: ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-meta:${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}
    container_name: beegfs-meta
    privileged: true
    network_mode: host
    depends_on:
      - beegfs-management
    command: >-
      storeMetaDirectory=/mnt/meta_01_tgt_0101
      storeAllowFirstRunInit=false
      sysMgmtdHost=127.0.0.1
      connMgmtdPortTCP=8008
      connMgmtdPortUDP=8008
      connMetaPortTCP=8005
      connMetaPortUDP=8005
    environment:
      - beegfs_setup_1=beegfs-setup-meta -C -p /mnt/meta_01_tgt_0101 -s 1 -S meta_01
    volumes:
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/meta_01_tgt_0101:/mnt/meta_01_tgt_0101

  beegfs-storage:
    image: ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-storage:${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}
    container_name: beegfs-storage
    privileged: true
    network_mode: host
    depends_on:
      - beegfs-management
    command: >-
      storeStorageDirectory=/mnt/stor_01_tgt_101,/mnt/stor_01_tgt_102
      storeAllowFirstRunInit=false
      sysMgmtdHost=127.0.0.1
      connMgmtdPortTCP=8008
      connMgmtdPortUDP=8008
      connStoragePortTCP=8003
      connStoragePortUDP=8003
    environment:
      - beegfs_setup_1=beegfs-setup-storage -C -p /mnt/stor_01_tgt_101 -s 1 -S stor_01_tgt_101 -i 101
      - beegfs_setup_2=beegfs-setup-storage -C -p /mnt/stor_01_tgt_102 -s 1 -S stor_01_tgt_101 -i 102
    volumes:
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/stor_01_tgt_101:/mnt/stor_01_tgt_101
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/stor_01_tgt_102:/mnt/stor_01_tgt_102

Two problems:
1. `beegfs-helperd` systemd unit reads `/etc/beegfs/beegfs-helperd.conf` (shipped default, has auth enabled) so it dies before we can use it — but `systemctl start` doesn't fail visibly, so we skipped our fallback.
2. The kernel mount's "sanity check" needs helperd on tcp/8006.

Fix: always start helperd manually with our test conf, skip systemd. Let me also verify helperd accepts the client conf format.

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Yaroslav Halchenko <yaroslav.o.halchenko@dartmouth.edu>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Generated with Claude Code 2.1.63 / Claude Opus 4.7
#
# Evaluate a command with TMPDIR / DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR (and optionally
# HOME) pointing at a BeeGFS mount, backed by a containerised BeeGFS cluster
# (mgmtd + meta + storage) brought up via docker compose.
#
# Modelled on datalad/datalad tools/eval_under_nfs -- same wrapper shape so
# CI usage matches: `eval_under_beegfs -- timeout 3600 git annex test`.
#
# Usage:
#   eval_under_beegfs [--keep] [--mount-point PATH] [--set-home] -- CMD [ARGS...]
#
#   --keep         skip teardown (leave containers + mount alive for debugging)
#   --mount-point  where to mount BeeGFS on host (default /mnt/beegfs)
#   --set-home     also set HOME=<mount-point>/home (mimics the git-annex
#                  build-ubuntu.yaml `*-home` flavors)
#
# Env vars:
#   BEEGFS_MOUNT         overrides --mount-point default (/mnt/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT     host dir for container-side target storage (/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG     image tag for ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-* (7.4.6)
#   BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT  seconds to wait for mgmtd to become reachable (60)
#
# Exit code == command's exit code. Teardown runs on any exit.

set -eu

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"

MNT="${BEEGFS_MOUNT:-/mnt/beegfs}"
DATA_ROOT="${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}"
COMPOSE="$repo_root/beegfs/docker-compose.yml"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$repo_root/beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template"
CONF_ACTIVE="/etc/beegfs/beegfs-client-test.conf"
STARTUP_WAIT="${BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT:-60}"
KEEP=0
SET_HOME=0

usage() {
  sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit "${1:-2}"
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    --mount-point) MNT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --set-home) SET_HOME=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage 0 ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; usage 2 ;;
  esac
done

[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "no command given" >&2; usage 2; }

if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
  command -v sudo >/dev/null || {
    echo "must run as root (or have sudo available)" >&2; exit 2; }
  SUDO=(sudo)
  SUDO_E=(sudo -E)
else
  SUDO=()
  SUDO_E=()
fi

log() { printf '\nI: %s\n' "$*"; }

ensure_client_installed() {
  if modinfo beegfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  echo "ERROR: beegfs kernel module not available." >&2
  echo "  Install with: apt install beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils" >&2
  exit 3
}

start_cluster() {
  log "creating data dirs under $DATA_ROOT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mkdir -p \
    "$DATA_ROOT/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/meta_01_tgt_0101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_102"

  log "docker compose up (BeeGFS ${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6})"
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
  BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG="${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}" \
    "${SUDO_E[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" up -d

  log "waiting up to ${STARTUP_WAIT}s for mgmtd on tcp/8008"
  local waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -lt "$STARTUP_WAIT" ]; do
    # mgmtd listens on 8008/tcp once initialised. `ss` is in iproute2.
    if "${SUDO[@]}" ss -ltn "sport = :8008" 2>/dev/null | grep -q :8008; then
      log "mgmtd is up (after ${waited}s)"
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
  done
  echo "ERROR: mgmtd did not come up within ${STARTUP_WAIT}s" >&2
  "${SUDO[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" logs --tail=200 >&2 || true
  exit 4
}

write_client_conf() {
  log "writing $CONF_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -d /etc/beegfs
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -m 0644 "$CONF_TEMPLATE" "$CONF_ACTIVE"
}

mount_beegfs() {
  log "starting beegfs-helperd"
  # helperd reads the same conf; point it at ours.
  "${SUDO[@]}" systemctl start beegfs-helperd || {
    # No systemd (e.g. inside `act` container): fall back to direct launch.
    "${SUDO[@]}" beegfs-helperd cfgFile="$CONF_ACTIVE" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    sleep 1
  }

  log "mounting BeeGFS at $MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mkdir -p "$MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mount -t beegfs beegfs_nodev "$MNT" -o "cfgFile=$CONF_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mount | grep -F "$MNT" | sed 's/^/I: /'
}

teardown() {
  local rc=$?
  set +e
  if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ]; then
    echo "I: --keep set; leaving cluster + mount up (exit=$rc)"
    return "$rc"
  fi
  log "teardown"
  "${SUDO[@]}" umount "$MNT" 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" systemctl stop beegfs-helperd 2>/dev/null \
    || "${SUDO[@]}" pkill -f beegfs-helperd || true
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
    "${SUDO_E[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" down -v 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" rm -rf "$DATA_ROOT" "$CONF_ACTIVE"
  return "$rc"
}
trap teardown EXIT

ensure_client_installed
start_cluster
write_client_conf
mount_beegfs

RUN_HOME="$HOME"
if [ "$SET_HOME" = 1 ]; then
  RUN_HOME="$MNT/home"
  mkdir -p "$RUN_HOME"
fi

log "running: $*"
HOME="$RUN_HOME" TMPDIR="$MNT" DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR="$MNT" "$@"

  echo "  Install with: apt install beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils" >&2
  exit 3
}

start_cluster() {
  log "creating data dirs under $DATA_ROOT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mkdir -p \
    "$DATA_ROOT/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/meta_01_tgt_0101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_102"

  log "docker compose up (BeeGFS ${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6})"
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
  BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG="${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}" \
    "${SUDO_E[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" up -d

  log "waiting up to ${STARTUP_WAIT}s for mgmtd on tcp/8008"
  local waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -lt "$STARTUP_WAIT" ]; do
    # mgmtd listens on 8008/tcp once initialised. `ss` is in iproute2.
    if "${SUDO[@]}" ss -ltn "sport = :8008" 2>/dev/null | grep -q :8008; then
      log "mgmtd is up (after ${waited}s)"
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
  done
  echo "ERROR: mgmtd did not come up within ${STARTUP_WAIT}s" >&2
  "${SUDO[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" logs --tail=200 >&2 || true
  exit 4
}

write_confs() {
  log "writing $CONF_ACTIVE + $HELPERD_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -d /etc/beegfs
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -m 0644 "$CONF_TEMPLATE"    "$CONF_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -m 0644 "$HELPERD_TEMPLATE" "$HELPERD_ACTIVE"
}

start_helperd() {
  # The shipped systemd unit reads /etc/beegfs/beegfs-helperd.conf, which
  # has auth enabled by default and would refuse to start. Bypass systemd
  # and launch helperd directly with our test conf. runDaemonized=true in
  # the conf means it forks and returns immediately.
  log "starting beegfs-helperd (direct, cfgFile=$HELPERD_ACTIVE)"
  "${SUDO[@]}" systemctl stop beegfs-helperd 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" "$HELPERD_BIN" "cfgFile=$HELPERD_ACTIVE"
  # Wait for port 8006 (timeout ~5s).
  local w=0
  while [ "$w" -lt 5 ]; do
    if "${SUDO[@]}" ss -ltn "sport = :8006" 2>/dev/null | grep -q :8006; then
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 1; w=$((w+1))
  done
  echo "ERROR: beegfs-helperd did not bind to tcp/8006" >&2
  "${SUDO[@]}" tail -50 /var/log/beegfs-helperd-test.log 2>&1 >&2 || true
  exit 5
}

mount_beegfs() {
  log "mounting BeeGFS at $MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mkdir -p "$MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mount -t beegfs beegfs_nodev "$MNT" -o "cfgFile=$CONF_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mount | grep -F "$MNT" | sed 's/^/I: /'
}

teardown() {
  local rc=$?
  set +e
  if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ]; then
    echo "I: --keep set; leaving cluster + mount up (exit=$rc)"
    return "$rc"
  fi
  log "teardown"
  "${SUDO[@]}" umount "$MNT" 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" systemctl stop beegfs-helperd 2>/dev/null \
    || "${SUDO[@]}" pkill -f beegfs-helperd || true
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
    "${SUDO_E[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" down -v 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" rm -rf "$DATA_ROOT" "$CONF_ACTIVE"
  return "$rc"
}
trap teardown EXIT

ensure_client_installed
start_cluster
write_confs
start_helperd
mount_beegfs

RUN_HOME="$HOME"
if [ "$SET_HOME" = 1 ]; then
  RUN_HOME="$MNT/home"
  mkdir -p "$RUN_HOME"
fi

log "running: $*"
HOME="$RUN_HOME" TMPDIR="$MNT" DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR="$MNT" "$@"

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Yaroslav Halchenko <yaroslav.o.halchenko@dartmouth.edu>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Generated with Claude Code 2.1.63 / Claude Opus 4.7
#
# Evaluate a command with TMPDIR / DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR (and optionally
# HOME) pointing at a BeeGFS mount, backed by a containerised BeeGFS cluster
# (mgmtd + meta + storage) brought up via docker compose.
#
# Modelled on datalad/datalad tools/eval_under_nfs -- same wrapper shape so
# CI usage matches: `eval_under_beegfs -- timeout 3600 git annex test`.
#
# Usage:
#   eval_under_beegfs [--keep] [--mount-point PATH] [--set-home] -- CMD [ARGS...]
#
#   --keep         skip teardown (leave containers + mount alive for debugging)
#   --mount-point  where to mount BeeGFS on host (default /mnt/beegfs)
#   --set-home     also set HOME=<mount-point>/home (mimics the git-annex
#                  build-ubuntu.yaml `*-home` flavors)
#
# Env vars:
#   BEEGFS_MOUNT         overrides --mount-point default (/mnt/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT     host dir for container-side target storage (/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG     image tag for ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-* (7.4.6)
#   BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT  seconds to wait for mgmtd to become reachable (60)
#
# Exit code == command's exit code. Teardown runs on any exit.

set -eu

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"

MNT="${BEEGFS_MOUNT:-/mnt/beegfs}"
DATA_ROOT="${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}"
COMPOSE="$repo_root/beegfs/docker-compose.yml"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$repo_root/beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template"
CONF_ACTIVE="/etc/beegfs/beegfs-client-test.conf"
HELPERD_TEMPLATE="$repo_root/beegfs/beegfs-helperd.conf.template"
HELPERD_ACTIVE="/etc/beegfs/beegfs-helperd-test.conf"
HELPERD_BIN="/opt/beegfs/sbin/beegfs-helperd"
STARTUP_WAIT="${BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT:-60}"
KEEP=0
SET_HOME=0

usage() {
  sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit "${1:-2}"
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    --mount-point) MNT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --set-home) SET_HOME=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage 0 ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; usage 2 ;;
  esac
done

[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "no command given" >&2; usage 2; }

if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
  command -v sudo >/dev/null || {
    echo "must run as root (or have sudo available)" >&2; exit 2; }
  SUDO=(sudo)
  SUDO_E=(sudo -E)
else
  SUDO=()
  SUDO_E=()
fi

log() { printf '\nI: %s\n' "$*"; }

ensure_client_installed() {
  if modinfo beegfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  echo "ERROR: beegfs kernel module not available." >&2
  echo "  Install with: apt install beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils" >&2
  exit 3
}

start_cluster() {
  log "creating data dirs under $DATA_ROOT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mkdir -p \
    "$DATA_ROOT/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/meta_01_tgt_0101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_102"

  log "docker compose up (BeeGFS ${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6})"
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
  BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG="${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}" \
    "${SUDO_E[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" up -d

  log "waiting up to ${STARTUP_WAIT}s for mgmtd on tcp/8008"
  local waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -lt "$STARTUP_WAIT" ]; do
    # mgmtd listens on 8008/tcp once initialised. `ss` is in iproute2.
    if "${SUDO[@]}" ss -ltn "sport = :8008" 2>/dev/null | grep -q :8008; then
      log "mgmtd is up (after ${waited}s)"
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
  done
  echo "ERROR: mgmtd did not come up within ${STARTUP_WAIT}s" >&2
  "${SUDO[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" logs --tail=200 >&2 || true
  exit 4
}

write_confs() {
  log "writing $CONF_ACTIVE + $HELPERD_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -d /etc/beegfs
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -m 0644 "$CONF_TEMPLATE"    "$CONF_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" install -m 0644 "$HELPERD_TEMPLATE" "$HELPERD_ACTIVE"
}

start_helperd() {
  # The shipped systemd unit reads /etc/beegfs/beegfs-helperd.conf, which
  # has auth enabled by default and would refuse to start. Bypass systemd
  # and launch helperd directly with our test conf. runDaemonized=true in
  # the conf means it forks and returns immediately.
  log "starting beegfs-helperd (direct, cfgFile=$HELPERD_ACTIVE)"
  "${SUDO[@]}" systemctl stop beegfs-helperd 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" "$HELPERD_BIN" "cfgFile=$HELPERD_ACTIVE"
  # Wait for port 8006 (timeout ~5s).
  local w=0
  while [ "$w" -lt 5 ]; do
    if "${SUDO[@]}" ss -ltn "sport = :8006" 2>/dev/null | grep -q :8006; then
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 1; w=$((w+1))
  done
  echo "ERROR: beegfs-helperd did not bind to tcp/8006" >&2
  "${SUDO[@]}" tail -50 /var/log/beegfs-helperd-test.log 2>&1 >&2 || true
  exit 5
}

mount_beegfs() {
  log "mounting BeeGFS at $MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mkdir -p "$MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mount -t beegfs beegfs_nodev "$MNT" -o "cfgFile=$CONF_ACTIVE"
  "${SUDO[@]}" chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$MNT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mount | grep -F "$MNT" | sed 's/^/I: /'
}

teardown() {
  local rc=$?
  set +e
  if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ]; then
    echo "I: --keep set; leaving cluster + mount up (exit=$rc)"
    return "$rc"
  fi
  log "teardown"
  "${SUDO[@]}" umount "$MNT" 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" pkill -f "$HELPERD_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
    "${SUDO_E[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" down -v 2>/dev/null || true
  "${SUDO[@]}" rm -rf "$DATA_ROOT" "$CONF_ACTIVE" "$HELPERD_ACTIVE"
  return "$rc"
}
trap teardown EXIT

ensure_client_installed
start_cluster
write_confs
start_helperd
mount_beegfs

RUN_HOME="$HOME"
if [ "$SET_HOME" = 1 ]; then
  RUN_HOME="$MNT/home"
  mkdir -p "$RUN_HOME"
fi

log "running: $*"
HOME="$RUN_HOME" TMPDIR="$MNT" DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR="$MNT" "$@"

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Yaroslav Halchenko <yaroslav.o.halchenko@dartmouth.edu>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Generated with Claude Code 2.1.63 / Claude Opus 4.7
#
# Provision an Ubuntu 24.04 VM to develop/test the beegfs-test harness:
#   - Docker CE + compose plugin
#   - BeeGFS client kernel module (DKMS) + helperd + utils
#   - git-annex + git (Ubuntu apt versions, enough to smoke-test the wrapper)
#
# Idempotent: safe to re-run via `vagrant provision`.

set -euo pipefail

BEEGFS_VERSION="${BEEGFS_VERSION:-7.4.6}"
# BeeGFS APT repo uses the full point-release in the path
# (e.g. beegfs_7.4.6/, not beegfs_7.4/).

log() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$*"; }

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

log "Base packages"
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release \
  build-essential dkms "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" \
  git git-annex jq

log "Docker CE + compose plugin"
if ! command -v docker >/dev/null; then
  install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
  curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg \
    -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
  echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $codename stable" \
    > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
fi
usermod -aG docker vagrant || true
systemctl enable --now docker

log "BeeGFS APT repo (v${BEEGFS_VERSION})"
# Prefer a list file for the current Ubuntu codename; fall back to jammy
# if the newer codename isn't yet published (BeeGFS DKMS still builds).
codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_VERSION}/dists/beegfs-${codename}.list"
if ! curl -fsI "$list_url" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "beegfs-${codename}.list not published upstream; falling back to jammy" >&2
  list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_VERSION}/dists/beegfs-jammy.list"
fi
curl -fsSL "$list_url" -o /etc/apt/sources.list.d/beegfs.list
curl -fsSL "https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_VERSION}/gpg/GPG-KEY-beegfs" \
  -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/beegfs.asc
apt-get update -qq

log "BeeGFS client (DKMS) + helperd + utils"
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils

# Verify the DKMS module built and is loadable. modprobe --dry-run avoids
# actually loading (that happens at mount time), so it's safe to fail-fast
# here if the module wasn't produced.
if ! modinfo beegfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: beegfs kernel module was not built by DKMS." >&2
  dkms status || true
  exit 1
fi

# helperd disabled by default — eval_under_beegfs starts it on demand.
systemctl disable --now beegfs-helperd || true

log "Provisioning complete"
echo "  git-annex : $(git-annex version | head -1)"
echo "  docker    : $(docker --version)"
echo "  beegfs mod: $(modinfo -F version beegfs 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"

Test is running in the VM (~10 min). I'll get pinged when it finishes.

Quick summary of what's working now (harness end-to-end validated via SMOKE_OK):

**Files staged:**
- `Vagrantfile` — libvirt ubuntu-24.04 with static IP `172.28.128.50`
- `provision/setup.sh` — docker CE, BeeGFS 7.4.6 DKMS (with retry-on-race), git-annex
- `provision/install-act.sh` — opt-in `act`
- `beegfs/docker-compose.yml` — v7 cluster, `network_mode: host`, `connDisableAuthentication=true`
- `beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template`
- `beegfs/beegfs-helperd.conf.template` (new)
- `tools/eval_under_beegfs` — waits for mgmtd+meta+storage all listening; direct-launches helperd (bypasses systemd unit that reads shipped conf); `sudo` handled via bash arrays for root+non-root
- `.github/workflows/smoke.yaml` + `drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml` — unchanged from earlier, still valid (will need the helperd template pulled in on the CI side but paths are ok)
- `README.md`

**Bugs found & fixed during smoke:**
1. Vagrant box `generic/ubuntu2404` retired → `cloud-image/ubuntu-24.04`
2. BeeGFS APT URL needed full point version, not major.minor
3. Missing second NIC on `vagrant reload` after Vagrantfile change → `destroy && up`
4. `$SUDO -E` expanded to `-E` when running as root → bash arrays
5. Compose services refused to start without `connDisableAuthentication=true`
6. Systemd `beegfs-helperd` reads shipped auth-enabled conf → launch helperd directly with our test conf
7. Race: mount happened before meta finished registering → wait for all three ports

I'll report the full-test result and the smoke workflow update path once the background test finishes.

- Vagrantfile + provisioners + `eval_under_beegfs` + docker-compose all working end-to-end

input.content:
Add harness for testing git-annex under BeeGFS

Establishes end-to-end machinery to run `git annex test` on a BeeGFS
mount, motivated by the 35+ test failures reported at
https://git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/ and the
open request in https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers/issues/21
for an example CI recipe.

Pieces:

* Vagrantfile + provision/setup.sh   -- libvirt Ubuntu 24.04 VM with
  Docker CE, BeeGFS 7.4.6 client kernel module (DKMS, with a retry
  around the flaky first-run postinst), and git-annex. Static private
  network IP 172.28.128.50 so the VM is reachable from Claude's dev
  container without vagrant ssh.
* provision/install-act.sh           -- opt-in nektos/act (VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT=1).
* beegfs/docker-compose.yml          -- BeeGFS v7 test cluster
  (mgmtd + meta + storage), pinned to 7.4.6, network_mode: host so
  the host-side kernel client can reach the services on localhost.
  connDisableAuthentication=true on all three services (throwaway
  test cluster, no secrets).
* beegfs/beegfs-{client,helperd}.conf.template -- minimal per-daemon
  configs (helperd's schema is distinct from client's; sharing one
  file errors out on unknown keys).
* tools/eval_under_beegfs            -- wrapper mirroring
  datalad/datalad tools/eval_under_nfs: stands up the cluster, mounts
  BeeGFS, runs the given command with TMPDIR / DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR
  (and optionally HOME via --set-home) pointing at the mount, tears
  down cleanly from a trap. Launches helperd directly (bypasses the
  shipped systemd unit that reads the auth-enabled default conf).
  Waits for mgmtd + meta + storage ports before mounting to avoid a
  registration race.
* .github/workflows/smoke.yaml       -- end-to-end sanity of the
  harness on a real ubuntu-24.04 GitHub runner.
* drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml  -- copy-target draft for
  datalad/git-annex CI, in-file notes on how to splice into
  build-ubuntu.yaml.

Validated on the VM: harness completes; `git annex test` against the
Ubuntu-shipped git-annex 10.20240129 reproduces the exact
"Device or resource busy" rename failure in the `export and import`
tests -- i.e. the harness catches the class of regression it was
designed to catch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code 2.1.233 / Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

**Bug confirmed to still exist in current git-annex 10.20260525** (fresh from datalad/git-annex releases). Same two tests fail with the same class of error:

```
git-annex: renamePath:rename '.git/annex/othertmp/213af7ee-93d8-4d.0/...'
  to '.git/annex/export.ex/...': resource busy (Device or resource busy)
```

- `export and import` — FAIL
- `export and import of subdir` — FAIL
- 51 other tests across 4 suites — PASS
- `EXIT=1`

The error signature has evolved slightly since the old version — it's now `renamePath:rename` with a HasCallStack backtrace pointing at `Messages.hs:375`. So this is a distinct code path that the earlier OsPath fix didn't cover (or a regression), and the harness would have surfaced it in CI on the day it landed.

**Net for you:**
- Harness works.
- Commit `cd878a1` is ready to push.
- The harness has real bug-finding value — this is not just theoretical CI insurance, current git-annex still trips on BeeGFS rename semantics, so a real regression is sitting in mainline waiting to be reported upstream.

Suggested follow-ups (your call):
1. Push the branch + open the `smoke.yaml` on a real GH runner.
2. File this reproducer as a fresh bug at git-annex.branchable.com (referencing the earlier one — this looks like an incomplete fix, since the same test names are still failing with a similar-but-not-identical error).
3. PR the harness upstream to `datalad/git-annex` from `drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml`.

name: BeeGFS harness smoke test

# Proves eval_under_beegfs works end-to-end on a real ubuntu-24.04 GH runner.
# Not a git-annex regression test -- that lives in the drafts/ workflow which
# is meant to be merged into datalad/git-annex.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
    paths:
      - "tools/**"
      - "beegfs/**"
      - "provision/**"
      - ".github/workflows/smoke.yaml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "tools/**"
      - "beegfs/**"
      - "provision/**"
      - ".github/workflows/smoke.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 5 * * 1"  # weekly Mon 05:17 UTC -- catches upstream image drift

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        beegfs-version: ["7.4.6"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install BeeGFS client (DKMS) + utils
        env:
          BEEGFS_VERSION: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          codename="$(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")"
          list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_VERSION}/dists/beegfs-${codename}.list"
          curl -fsI "$list_url" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || list_url="https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_VERSION}/dists/beegfs-jammy.list"
          sudo curl -fsSL "$list_url" -o /etc/apt/sources.list.d/beegfs.list
          sudo curl -fsSL "https://www.beegfs.io/release/beegfs_${BEEGFS_VERSION}/gpg/GPG-KEY-beegfs" \
            -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/beegfs.asc
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            dkms "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" \
            beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils
          modinfo beegfs

      - name: Install git-annex
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git-annex
          git-annex version | head -3

      - name: Smoke-test eval_under_beegfs
        env:
          BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG: ${{ matrix.beegfs-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo -E ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- bash -eu -c '
            echo "HOME=$HOME  TMPDIR=$TMPDIR"
            mount | grep -F "$TMPDIR"
            cd "$HOME"
            git config --global user.email test@example.com
            git config --global user.name  test
            git init t
            cd t
            git annex init smoke
            dd if=/dev/urandom of=big bs=1M count=10 status=none
            git annex add big
            git commit -m "add big"
            git annex fsck
            echo OK
          '

      - name: Container logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: sudo docker compose -f beegfs/docker-compose.yml logs --tail=500 || true

      - name: Install git-annex (apt; draft only)

Add harness for testing git-annex under BeeGFS

Establishes end-to-end machinery to run `git annex test` on a BeeGFS
mount, motivated by the 35+ test failures reported at
https://git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/ and the
open request in https://github.com/ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers/issues/21
for an example CI recipe.

Pieces:

* Vagrantfile + provision/setup.sh   -- libvirt Ubuntu 24.04 VM with
  Docker CE, BeeGFS 7.4.6 client kernel module (DKMS, with a retry
  around the flaky first-run postinst), and git-annex. Static private
  network IP 172.28.128.50 so the VM is reachable from Claude's dev
  container without vagrant ssh.
* provision/install-act.sh           -- opt-in nektos/act (VAGRANT_INSTALL_ACT=1).
* beegfs/docker-compose.yml          -- BeeGFS v7 test cluster
  (mgmtd + meta + storage), pinned to 7.4.6, network_mode: host so
  the host-side kernel client can reach the services on localhost.
  connDisableAuthentication=true on all three services (throwaway
  test cluster, no secrets).
* beegfs/beegfs-{client,helperd}.conf.template -- minimal per-daemon
  configs (helperd's schema is distinct from client's; sharing one
  file errors out on unknown keys).
* tools/eval_under_beegfs            -- wrapper mirroring
  datalad/datalad tools/eval_under_nfs: stands up the cluster, mounts
  BeeGFS, runs the given command with TMPDIR / DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR
  (and optionally HOME via --set-home) pointing at the mount, tears
  down cleanly from a trap. Launches helperd directly (bypasses the
  shipped systemd unit that reads the auth-enabled default conf).
  Waits for mgmtd + meta + storage ports before mounting to avoid a
  registration race.
* .github/workflows/smoke.yaml       -- end-to-end sanity of the
  harness on a real ubuntu-24.04 GitHub runner.
* drafts/git-annex-test-beegfs.yaml  -- copy-target draft for
  datalad/git-annex CI, in-file notes on how to splice into
  build-ubuntu.yaml.

Validated on the VM: harness completes; `git annex test` against the
Ubuntu-shipped git-annex 10.20240129 reproduces the exact
"Device or resource busy" rename failure in the `export and import`
tests -- i.e. the harness catches the class of regression it was
designed to catch.

content.text:
Understood — nothing filed by me. Here's what you need to reproduce and what the report should contain.

## Minimal reproducer (run in the VM)

Targeted invocation — runs only the failing test in ~1 minute instead of the full 15-min suite:

```bash
vagrant ssh -c 'set -eu; cd /vagrant && sudo -E ./tools/eval_under_beegfs --set-home -- bash -c "
  export PATH=/usr/lib/git-annex.linux:\$PATH
  cd \$HOME
  git config --global user.email t@t
  git config --global user.name  t
  git annex version | head -1
  git annex test -p \"/export and import/\"
"'
```

If it fails with `renamePath:rename '.git/annex/othertmp/…' … resource busy (Device or resource busy)` — reproduced.

## Environment matters — capture these

Put the output of these inside the report (BeeGFS filesystem semantics differ from most FSes, and reporters routinely omit these):

```bash
vagrant ssh -c '
  echo "=== OS ==="            && lsb_release -a
  echo "=== kernel ==="        && uname -a
  echo "=== git-annex ==="     && git annex version | head -5
  echo "=== beegfs kmod ==="   && modinfo -F version beegfs
  echo "=== beegfs client ==="; dpkg -l beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-utils | tail -3
  echo "=== mount ==="; mount | grep beegfs
  echo "=== beegfs-ctl ==="; sudo beegfs-ctl --listnodes --nodetype=meta 2>&1 | head
'
```

## What to file at git-annex.branchable.com

The existing bug page is <https://git-annex.branchable.com/bugs/35_failed_tests_on_beegfs/> and it's marked resolved via the OsPath / `O_CLOEXEC` fix. What you're seeing suggests either:

- an **incomplete** fix (this specific `renamePath` call site was missed), or
- a **regression** (something re-introduced a non-cloexec open in this code path).

Suggested framing — post as a *new* bug with a link to the old one (not a comment on the old one, since it's marked done), title along the lines of:

> "export and import" test still fails on BeeGFS with `renamePath: resource busy` (follow-up to #35_failed_tests_on_beegfs)

Body should include:

1. **One-sentence claim.** "git-annex 10.20260525's `git annex test -p '/export and import/'` reproducibly fails on a BeeGFS 7.4.6 mount with `renamePath:rename … resource busy`, same class of failure as the earlier bug report but distinct code path."
2. **Link to old bug** so the reader has the OsPath context.
3. **Reproducer** — the `eval_under_beegfs` one-liner above, or a link to `https://github.com/yarikoptic/beegfs-test` once you're comfortable pointing at it.
4. **Failing test transcript** — the block ending with:

   ```
   git-annex: renamePath:rename '.git/annex/othertmp/213af7ee-93d8-4d.0/213af7ee-93d8-4d'
     to '.git/annex/export.ex/213af7ee-93d8-4d8b-a51f-125498100514':
     resource busy (Device or resource busy)
   HasCallStack backtrace:
     collectBacktraces, called at libraries/ghc-internal/src/GHC/Internal/Exception.hs:169:13
     …
     throwM, called at Messages.hs:375:17 in git-annex-10.20260525-…-git-annex:Messages
   ```

   (The `Messages.hs:375` reference is Joey's most useful breadcrumb — it points at the exception-throw site, and from there `git grep renamePath` in git-annex sources will locate the actual open+rename pair that leaks the fd.)
5. **Environment block** from the previous command.
6. **Hypothesis** — "Looks like the `renamePath` call in `Annex/Export/…` (or wherever the `.git/annex/othertmp/ → .git/annex/export.ex/` move happens) doesn't go through the OsPath-based helper that received the `O_CLOEXEC` fix, so a child process (probably `git cat-file --batch` opened by the export logic) still holds the fd across the rename."
7. **What you have NOT tested** — say so explicitly:
   - Only tried git-annex 10.20260525 (datalad build). Not tried joeyh's latest daily.
   - Only tried BeeGFS 7.4.6. Not tried 7.4.7 (published upstream, may or may not change behaviour) or 8.x.
   - Only tried Ubuntu 22.04 host, kernel 5.15.

Being explicit about what you didn't test saves Joey a round trip.

## Before filing — the "did I really reproduce it" checklist

1. **Different git-annex version:** try joeyh's daily upstream (not the datalad build). If it also fails, the bug is upstream, not in the datalad packaging. Their APT is at `https://downloads.kitenet.net/git-annex/linux/current/` — grab the tarball and run its bundled `git-annex` under `eval_under_beegfs`. If ONLY the datalad build fails, it's a build/packaging issue and reporting to datalad/git-annex issues is more appropriate than branchable.com.
2. **Different BeeGFS version:** try `BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG=7.4.7 sudo -E ./tools/eval_under_beegfs …`. If 7.4.7 passes and 7.4.6 fails, it's a BeeGFS 7.4.6-specific bug — report to ThinkParQ instead of git-annex.
3. **Rerun 2–3 times.** Confirm it's not flaky.

Say the word if you want me to do step (1) or (2) for you in the VM before you file.

input.content:
# BeeGFS v8 test cluster for eval_under_beegfs.
#
# Derived from ThinkParQ/beegfs-containers examples/docker-compose-v8.yml,
# modified for host-mode networking so the beegfs kernel client on the
# host can reach mgmtd/meta/storage on localhost. v8 replaces v7's
# "confstring" command style with proper flags and adds a gRPC control
# plane on 8010; legacy TCP/UDP messaging still runs on 8008/8005/8003.
#
# BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT (default /beegfs) chooses where target dirs live on host.
# BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG pins the ghcr.io/thinkparq/* image tag (default 8.1.0).

services:
  beegfs-management:
    image: ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-mgmtd:${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-8.1.0}
    container_name: beegfs-mgmtd
    privileged: true
    network_mode: host
    command: >-
      --db-file /mnt/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01/mgmtd.sqlite
      --log-target stderr
      --tls-disable true
      --auth-disable true
    environment:
      - beegfs_setup_1=beegfs-mgmtd --init --db-file /mnt/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01/mgmtd.sqlite --log-target stderr
    volumes:
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01:/mnt/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01

  beegfs-meta:
    image: ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-meta:${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-8.1.0}
    container_name: beegfs-meta
    privileged: true
    network_mode: host
    depends_on:
      - beegfs-management
    # v8 meta still accepts the legacy confstring for compatibility --
    # gRPC control-plane bits (sysMgmtdHost via gRPC on 8010) are
    # negotiated automatically when it registers.
    command: >-
      storeMetaDirectory=/mnt/meta_01_tgt_0101
      storeAllowFirstRunInit=false
      sysMgmtdHost=127.0.0.1
      connMgmtdPortTCP=8008
      connMgmtdPortUDP=8008
      connMetaPortTCP=8005
      connMetaPortUDP=8005
      connDisableAuthentication=true
    environment:
      - beegfs_setup_1=beegfs-setup-meta -C -p /mnt/meta_01_tgt_0101 -s 1 -S meta_01
    volumes:
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/meta_01_tgt_0101:/mnt/meta_01_tgt_0101

  beegfs-storage:
    image: ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-storage:${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-8.1.0}
    container_name: beegfs-storage
    privileged: true
    network_mode: host
    depends_on:
      - beegfs-management
    command: >-
      storeStorageDirectory=/mnt/stor_01_tgt_101,/mnt/stor_01_tgt_102
      storeAllowFirstRunInit=false
      sysMgmtdHost=127.0.0.1
      connMgmtdPortTCP=8008
      connMgmtdPortUDP=8008
      connStoragePortTCP=8003
      connStoragePortUDP=8003
      connDisableAuthentication=true
    environment:
      - beegfs_setup_1=beegfs-setup-storage -C -p /mnt/stor_01_tgt_101 -s 1 -S stor_01_tgt_101 -i 101
      - beegfs_setup_2=beegfs-setup-storage -C -p /mnt/stor_01_tgt_102 -s 1 -S stor_01_tgt_101 -i 102
    volumes:
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/stor_01_tgt_101:/mnt/stor_01_tgt_101
      - ${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}/stor_01_tgt_102:/mnt/stor_01_tgt_102

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Yaroslav Halchenko <yaroslav.o.halchenko@dartmouth.edu>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Generated with Claude Code 2.1.63 / Claude Opus 4.7
#
# Evaluate a command with TMPDIR / DATALAD_TESTS_TEMP_DIR (and optionally
# HOME) pointing at a BeeGFS mount, backed by a containerised BeeGFS cluster
# (mgmtd + meta + storage) brought up via docker compose.
#
# Modelled on datalad/datalad tools/eval_under_nfs -- same wrapper shape so
# CI usage matches: `eval_under_beegfs -- timeout 3600 git annex test`.
#
# Usage:
#   eval_under_beegfs [--keep] [--mount-point PATH] [--set-home] -- CMD [ARGS...]
#
#   --keep         skip teardown (leave containers + mount alive for debugging)
#   --mount-point  where to mount BeeGFS on host (default /mnt/beegfs)
#   --set-home     also set HOME=<mount-point>/home (mimics the git-annex
#                  build-ubuntu.yaml `*-home` flavors)
#
# Env vars:
#   BEEGFS_MOUNT         overrides --mount-point default (/mnt/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT     host dir for container-side target storage (/beegfs)
#   BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG     image tag for ghcr.io/thinkparq/beegfs-* (7.4.6)
#   BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT  seconds to wait for mgmtd to become reachable (60)
#
# Exit code == command's exit code. Teardown runs on any exit.

set -eu

here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"

MNT="${BEEGFS_MOUNT:-/mnt/beegfs}"
DATA_ROOT="${BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT:-/beegfs}"
COMPOSE="$repo_root/beegfs/docker-compose.yml"
CONF_TEMPLATE="$repo_root/beegfs/beegfs-client.conf.template"
CONF_ACTIVE="/etc/beegfs/beegfs-client-test.conf"
HELPERD_TEMPLATE="$repo_root/beegfs/beegfs-helperd.conf.template"
HELPERD_ACTIVE="/etc/beegfs/beegfs-helperd-test.conf"
HELPERD_BIN="/opt/beegfs/sbin/beegfs-helperd"
STARTUP_WAIT="${BEEGFS_STARTUP_WAIT:-60}"
KEEP=0
SET_HOME=0

usage() {
  sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit "${1:-2}"
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    --mount-point) MNT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --set-home) SET_HOME=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage 0 ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; usage 2 ;;
  esac
done

[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "no command given" >&2; usage 2; }

if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
  command -v sudo >/dev/null || {
    echo "must run as root (or have sudo available)" >&2; exit 2; }
  SUDO=(sudo)
  SUDO_E=(sudo -E)
else
  SUDO=()
  SUDO_E=()
fi

log() { printf '\nI: %s\n' "$*"; }

ensure_client_installed() {
  if modinfo beegfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  echo "ERROR: beegfs kernel module not available." >&2
  echo "  Install with: apt install beegfs-client-dkms beegfs-helperd beegfs-utils" >&2
  exit 3
}

start_cluster() {
  log "creating data dirs under $DATA_ROOT"
  "${SUDO[@]}" mkdir -p \
    "$DATA_ROOT/mgmt_tgt_mgmt01" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/meta_01_tgt_0101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_101" \
    "$DATA_ROOT/stor_01_tgt_102"

  log "docker compose up (BeeGFS ${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6})"
  BEEGFS_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" \
  BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG="${BEEGFS_IMAGE_TAG:-7.4.6}" \
    "${SUDO_E[@]}" docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" up -d

  log "waiting up to ${STARTUP_WAIT}s for mgmtd(8008) + meta(8005) + storage(8003)"
  # All three must be listening AND meta must have registered with mgmtd
  # (mount sanity check queries the root metadata node). Waiting on the
  # meta TCP port is a reasonable proxy since meta binds after registering.
  local waited=0
  while [ "$waited" -lt "$STARTUP_WAIT" ]; do
    local ports
    ports=$("${SUDO[@]}" ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $4}' | awk -F: '{print $NF}')
    if grep -qx 8008 <<<"$ports" \
      && grep -qx 8005 <<<"$ports" \
      && grep -qx 8003 <<<"$ports"; then
      log "cluster is up (after ${waited}s)"
      # Small extra grace period for meta to finish node registration.
      sleep 2
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
